name: Book Club Radio
insight: YouTube DJ-set channel and party brand (also called BCR or Book Club) that films themed sets, for example a Gothic dance and EBM set by Georgi in a castle setting. Fans call it world-class and play it in heavy rotation. It runs a festival in Brooklyn, USA. Fans in other countries say they envy people who can attend in person.
examples: Fan compares the channel to the 1990s Miami Bass DJ scene and says every DJ on it moves them
Listener says Book Club makes slow work days better
Fan on the other side of the world feels FOMO about not having BCR nearby
Georgi's earlier Book Club set is still in a fan's heavy rotation
Black-and-red themed Book Club editions are seen as a sign of a good night
use: Attend: the channel announced the Book Club Radio Music Festival in Brooklyn on October 2nd and 3rd, with tickets on shotgun.live. For playing or submitting, check the outlet's own page.

name: VAMPIRA'S FRIDAY PLAYLIST
insight: Long-running YouTube radio stream and playlist of darkwave, post-punk, goth and coldwave, branded 'NO AI MUSIC'. Listeners thank it mainly for being human-made music at a time when AI playlists flood YouTube. People use it for studying and for songwriting inspiration. Listeners write in from Mexico and Liverpool, UK.
examples: Listener relieved to find real human-made music
Another says the number of AI playlists is driving them crazy
Used to track study time
A musician plans to use it as an influence
Complaints about frequent commercials
One commenter suggests a song for the playlist in the comments

name: Márian (dark disco, ebm, italo disco mix series)
insight: YouTube mix series mixing dark disco, EBM and italo disco, now at mix XV. Loyal fans play each new mix from start to finish the moment it appears, share it with friends and ask for track IDs.
examples: Fan says a new Marian mix is an instant play
Listener has shown the mixes to many friends
Mixes used as background while working
Track ID request for a specific timestamp

name: NTS
insight: Radio station with YouTube series such as 'THE NTS GUIDE TO…' and guest selections, for example Nabihah Iqbal's post-punk, new wave and no wave set. Fans praise its careful curation and its deep cuts, such as the Brazilian band Mercenárias and Wipers. One fan knows Nabihah from working the door at Bunker Club.
examples: Listener values songs curated with care and attention
Brazilian fans celebrate Mercenárias being included
Another 'banger mix' from the NTS guide series
Fan plans to check out the DJ's own album after the mix

name: B/A producciones
insight: YouTube DJ channel that hosts coldwave, EBM and new beat sets, such as 'It's electric where you find it' with Maggie Rollins. Fans call it the best DJ channel on YouTube and play at least one video a day. It has a strong Latin American audience in Mexico, Peru, Argentina and Brazil.
examples: Viewer found the channel last year and now plays a video daily while working
Commenter calls it the best DJ channel on YouTube
Brazilian fan asks the channel to keep going
Fan says it is always a hit when B/A producciones invites Maggie Rollins

name: DARK WAVE MIX | BEST PLAYLIST MIX 2026
insight: YouTube mix of dark synthwave, goth and coldwave with a 'vamp girl' visual. Many listeners say the thumbnail or an ad brought them in and the music kept them. They keep asking for single tracks on Spotify and YouTube Music. Its own pinned comment points to a DollWave Patreon for album downloads.
examples: Several listeners came for the vamp girl visual and stayed for the music
Found through an ad or YouTube recommendations
Requests to put specific songs on Spotify
Fan glad the set finally came out on YouTube Music as a separate album

name: Demand for human-made, non-AI music
insight: Across darkwave and NTS comments, several listeners explicitly reward channels for featuring real human musicians rather than AI-generated playlists. 'Human-made' works as a recommendation signal in itself.
examples: Thanks for real human-made music
Annoyed by the flood of AI playlists on YouTube
Praise for actual human musicians instead of prompts

name: Aether Sounds
insight: YouTube channel releasing melancholic darkwave, coldwave and minimal wave albums and mixes, for example 'Where the Shapes Dissolve'. Returning fans wait for each new album and go back to older ones such as Midnight Aether.
examples: Fan says a new album helps them get through the dark season
German-speaking listener follows every album and revisits older ones

name: Listeners want mix tracks on streaming platforms
insight: Fans of YouTube darkwave mixes repeatedly ask for individual tracks or whole sets on Spotify and YouTube Music so they can add them to their own playlists.
examples: Wishes the playlist were on YouTube Music
Needs specific songs on Spotify
Says the tracks must go into their Spotify playlist
Asks daily for one song as a standalone release

name: Club scenes remembered by listeners (Belgian clubs, German goth clubs, Camden, Bunker Club)
insight: Older fans link EBM and coldwave sets to physical club scenes they went to: Belgian clubs, German goth clubs, alternative clubs in Camden (UK) and Bunker Club. These are nostalgia references rather than current recommendations.
examples: Fan aged 64 went to Belgian clubs for this music at 18
Mix recalls German goth clubs of 15–20 years ago
Brazilian fan danced to this mix of genres in Camden clubs
Commenter met the DJ at the door of Bunker Club
